newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Dealers see new BEL-20 records in coming weeks.
newsitem.headline: Dealers see new BEL-20 records in coming weeks.

text.p: The Brussels bourse closed higher on Thursday as investors decided not to follow the Dow's overnight drop. Dealers said the index was on course to rise into record levels in coming weeks.
"There's no reason to expect the market to fall in the near future," one dealer said.
"We remain positive," he added. Dealers said low inflation and interest rates and favourable forecast for 1997 economic growth meant the bourse saw no obstacles to futher rises.
The Bel-20 share index .BFX closed up 0.45 percent or 8.44 points at 1,878.03 after Wednesday's 1,869.50 close.

Trade was thin with around two billion francs worth of shares (Belgian shares only) changing hands. Few investors were taking profits, sitting instead on their stocks and banking on the index to rise further.
"We saw diverse trading today but volume was low," said a dealer.
Insurance group Fortis AG shares were active and volatile, helping push up the index after it posted an 18 percent net profit increase for the first nine months to 554 million Ecus ($696.7 million).
